comments.body:
Thanks for fixing the tool-call parsing and adding tests! I checked the slide edit agent’s two-turn flow with the pinned Ollama SDK (0.6.1) and a mocked HTTP transport. The first tool call parses correctly. On the follow-up `/api/chat` request, the SDK drops `tool_call_id`, so the tool result reaches Ollama with only `role` and `content`.

Could you look up the original function name from the preceding assistant tool calls and send it as `tool_name` on the tool result? That’s the field Ollama uses to identify the tool that ran. A two-turn regression test that checks the serialized request body would cover this. Thanks!

[Ollama tool calling docs](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/tool-calling)

Thanks for checking the two-turn flow. Pushed a follow-up commit: tool results now carry `tool_name`, looked up from the preceding assistant tool calls (matched by `tool_call_id`, falling back to `AIMessage.name`). I added a two-turn regression test that runs the real `ollama.AsyncClient` over an `httpx.MockTransport` and asserts the serialized `/api/chat` body contains `tool_name: "edit_slide"` on the tool message; it fails without the change and passes with it.

This reply was drafted with Claude Code (AI-assisted) and posted on the author's behalf.
